You are implementing part of an original, from-scratch C re-implementation of the
command-line audio tool at /workspace/executable (self-identifies as "SoX v14.4.2").

CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole project):
 - Learn behaviour ONLY by RUNNING /workspace/executable and reading the bundled
   man pages /workspace/sox.1, /workspace/soxformat.7, /workspace/libsox.3, README.md.
 - NEVER search the web, fetch/clone/download upstream source, use a package
   manager to obtain the project, or read any copy of the original sources.
 - NEVER run objdump/gdb/ghidra/strace/ltrace/nm/readelf/strings on the binary.
 - Write ORIGINAL code; derive behaviour from experiments.

Read FIRST: /workspace/notes/CONTRACT.md, /workspace/notes/driver.md (a detailed
record of already-measured reference behaviour -- trust it, and extend it),
/workspace/src/sox.h, /workspace/src/sox_i.h.

sox.h/sox_i.h are the fixed contract. You may ADD declarations but never change
or remove existing ones -- other agents compile against them concurrently.

ONLY create/modify the files assigned to you (plus notes/*.md you own).
Never run 'git' write commands.

Other modules are still stubs, so a full link will fail. Check your file with:
    cc -c -std=gnu99 -I/workspace/src -O2 -Wall /workspace/src/YOURFILE.c -o /tmp/o.o
Iterate until it compiles cleanly.

Final message: a SHORT report (< 30 lines) of what you implemented, what you
could not determine, and any header additions.


YOUR ASSIGNMENT (only these files: src/formats.c)

Implement /workspace/src/formats.c: the format registry and the
sox_open_read / sox_open_write / sox_read / sox_write / sox_close / sox_seek API
declared in sox.h, plus sox_init/sox_quit/sox_format_init/sox_format_quit,
lsx_set_signal_defaults, the sox_encodings_info table is owned by util.c (do NOT
define it), and the help output for formats.

Responsibilities:

1. Build the handler table from src/formats.h (each lsx_<mod>_format_fn(); skip
   the ones that currently return NULL). Look up handlers by name
   case-insensitively across every name in handler->names.

2. File-type determination for input:
   a. an explicit -t/--type name;
   b. otherwise sniff the header ("magic") -- the reference reports
      'INFO formats: detected file format type `wav'' at -V3. Determine which
      formats are detected by magic and the exact byte signatures by creating a
      file of each type with the reference and then reading it back with a
      mismatched extension, e.g.
        ./executable -n -r 8000 f.dat synth 0.01 sin 300   # then
        cp f.dat g.bin && ./executable -V3 --i g.bin
      Cover at least: wav (RIFF/RIFX), aiff/aifc (FORM), au (.snd), sox (.SoX),
      voc (Creative Voice File), sph/nist (NIST_1A), 8svx (FORM..8SVX),
      maud (FORM..MAUD), smp (SOUND SAMPLE DATA), avr (2BIT), sndt, dvms/cvsd,
      hcom, txw, wve (ALawSoundFile**), gsrt, prc, xa, dat (starts with ';'),
      htk. Record exactly which ones are magic-detected and which are only
      recognised by extension in /workspace/notes/magic.md.
   c. otherwise the filename extension;
   d. failing that: 'FAIL formats: can't determine type of file `X''.
   Note the reference has a --no-glob option and expands wildcards in input
   names, and supports "|command" and "http://" inputs -- the driver handles
   those, not you.

3. sox_open_read(path, signal, encoding, filetype):
   - "-" means stdin. Open the file, allocate the sox_format_t and its priv,
     copy in any user-supplied signal/encoding overrides, call handler->startread,
     then fill in defaults. On failure print
       'FAIL formats: can't open input file `X': <strerror>'
     and return NULL. Set ft->seekable appropriately.
   - After startread, ft->signal.precision must be set via lsx_precision() if the
     handler left it 0.
4. sox_open_write(path, signal, encoding, filetype, comments, overwrite_permitted):
   - "-" means stdout. Honour the overwrite_permitted callback (used by
     --no-clobber; determine the exact prompt text from the reference by running
     './executable --no-clobber existing.wav existing2.wav' with an existing
     output). Print 'FAIL formats: can't open output file `X': <strerror>' on
     failure.
   - Check the handler's channel/rate restrictions (see --help-format output:
     "Channels restricted to: mono stereo", "Sample-rate restricted to: 44100").
     Determine the exact error/warning the reference gives when violated, e.g.
       ./executable stereo.wav -t cvsd out.cvsd
       ./executable -r 22050 in.wav -t cdda out.cdr
     and reproduce it.
5. sox_read/sox_write: call the handler, apply ft->signal.mult (the -v volume
   factor) on read if set, accumulate ft->clips, track ft->olength.
6. sox_close: call stopread/stopwrite, close the file (unless it is stdin/stdout).
7. sox_seek(ft, offset, SOX_SEEK_SET): delegate to handler->seek.
8. Help output. Implement two functions (declare them in sox_i.h):
       void lsx_display_supported_formats(void);   /* the AUDIO FILE FORMATS,
             PLAYLIST FORMATS and AUDIO DEVICE DRIVERS lines of './executable -h' */
       int lsx_usage_format(char const *name);     /* './executable --help-format X' */
   The formats line is the sorted (by strcmp) list of every name of every
   non-phony handler; check byte-for-byte against './executable -h'. Reproduce
   '--help-format=all' and '--help-format wav' exactly (see the reference).
   PLAYLIST FORMATS is the fixed list 'm3u pls'; AUDIO DEVICE DRIVERS is
   'oss ossdsp'.
   Also provide char const *lsx_encoding_name(sox_encoding_t, unsigned bits) style
   helper used to print '16-bit Signed Integer PCM' / '8-bit u-law' /
   'Floating Point (text) PCM' / 'LPC10' -- note encodings with no bit prefix.

9. Implement the output-encoding-selection helper described in
   /workspace/notes/driver.md section "Output encoding selection" as
       void lsx_choose_encoding(sox_format_handler_t const *h,
                                sox_encodinginfo_t *enc, unsigned target_precision);
   (declare in sox_i.h) so the driver can call it. Re-verify the rules with your
   own matrix of experiments and refine them if they are not exactly right.

Do not implement the individual formats; they are separate files owned by others.

10	`compile.sh` compiles every `src/**/*.c` into `./executable`.  Just add new `.c`
11	files under `src/`; no build file edits needed.  Compile with:

16	
17	* C99, no external libraries other than libm and libpthread.
18	* `#include "sox_i.h"` gives you everything (it includes `sox.h`).
19	* Internal linkage for everything except the one exported symbol per module.

73	    -p	Show estimated sample precision in bits
74	    -e	Show the name of the audio encoding
75	    -a	Show file comments (annotations) if available
76	
77	    With no options, as much information as is available is shown for
78	    each given file.
79	
80	(tabs after the option letters).  Single-value outputs, one line per file:
81	`-t`→`wav`, `-r`→`44100`, `-c`→`2`, `-s`→`44100`, `-d`→`00:00:01.00`,
82	`-D`→`1.000000`, `-b`→`16`, `-B`→`1.41M`, `-p`→`16`, `-e`→`Signed Integer PCM`,
83	`-a`→the comments.  With `-T` and `-s`/`-d`/`-D` a single total is printed
84	instead; `-T -s` prints the total as a float (`44180.000000`).
85	
86	## File info block
87	
88	Printed as `"\n"` + lines + `"\n"`, so consecutive blocks are separated by a
89	blank line.  Field name is padded to 15 chars then `": "`:
90	
91	    (blank)
92	    Input File     : 'st.wav'
93	    Channels       : 2
94	    Sample Rate    : 44100
95	    Precision      : 16-bit
96	    Duration       : 00:00:01.00 = 44100 samples = 75 CDDA sectors
97	    File Size      : 176k
98	    Bit Rate       : 1.41M
99	    Sample Encoding: 16-bit Signed Integer PCM
100	    Endian Type    : little            <- only at verbosity >= 3
101	    Reverse Nibbles: no                <- only at verbosity >= 3
102	    Reverse Bits   : no                <- only at verbosity >= 3
103	    Comment        : 'Processed by SoX'
104	    (blank)
105	
106	Output block header is `Output File    : 'out.au'`; a ` (type)` suffix is
107	appended when the file name's extension does not name the chosen handler (any of
108	its names counts, so `o.s16` with `-t s16` gets no suffix but `/dev/null` with
109	`-t s16` gets ` (s2)` and `o.xyz` with `-t aiff` gets ` (aiff)`).  Output blocks
110	have no `File Size`/`Bit Rate` lines.
111	
112	`Duration`/`File Size`/`Bit Rate` are all omitted when the length is unknown or
113	zero.  `Duration` = `hh:mm:ss.ss = N samples <sep> S CDDA sectors` where N is
114	samples-per-channel, S = seconds * 75 printed with `%g`, and `<sep>` is `=` when
115	S is an exact integer, `~` otherwise.
116	
117	`Comment        : '<text>'` for exactly one comment; for two or more:
118	
119	    Comments       : 
120	    a
121	    b
122	
123	(note the trailing space after the colon).  No comment line at all when the
124	comment is empty.
125	
126	`Total Duration of 2 files: 00:00:01.01` is printed after the last block when
127	soxi is given more than one file and no option letter.
128	
129	## 3-significant-figure formatting (`lsx_sigfigs3`)
130	
131	Units are powers of 1000 (`k`, `M`, `G`): value/unit printed with 3 significant
132	figures — `%.0f` when >= 100, `%.1f` when >= 10, `%.2f` otherwise.  Verified:
133	204→`204`, 163200→`163k`, 128000→`128k`, 535272→`535k`, 176444→`176k`,
134	1411552→`1.41M`, 44100→`44.1k`, 352800→`353k`, 8000→`8.00k`, 0→`0`.
135	Bit Rate = file_size_bytes * 8 / duration_seconds.
136	
137	Percentages (`lsx_sigfigs3p`): `0.00%`, `100%`.
138	
139	## Progress meter (`-S`; off by default when stderr is not a tty)
140	
141	    \rIn:0.00% 00:00:00.00 [00:00:01.00] Out:0     [      |      ]        Clip:0    
142	    \rIn:100%  00:00:01.00 [00:00:00.00] Out:44.1k [ =====|===== ]        Clip:0    
143	    Done.\n
144	
145	Layout: `"\rIn:%-5s %s [%s] Out:%-5s [%6s|%-6s] %-8s Clip:%-5" PRIu64` with the
146	last-but-one field empty in every case observed.  The two VU strings are mirror
147	images; the right-hand one as a function of the block's peak level:
148	
149	    -1dB "=====!"   -2/-3 "======"   -4/-5 "=====-"   -6/-7 "===== "
150	    -8/-9 "====- "  -10/-11 "====  " -12/-13 "===-  " -14 "===   "
151	    -15..-17 "==-   " -18/-19 "==    " -20/-21 "=-    " -22/-23 "=     "
152	    -24/-25 "-     " <= -26 "      "
153	    (0 dB and above shows "=====-" mirrored, i.e. left "-=====")
154	
155	`Done.` is printed on the line after the last meter update.
156	
157	## Output encoding selection (verified over a large matrix)
158	
159	Let `P` = the *input* signal's precision (before any effects).  Then:
160	
161	1. If the user gave both `-e` and `-b` and the handler supports the combination,
162	   use it.
163	2. If the user gave `-e` only: restrict candidates to that encoding.
164	   If the user gave `-b` only: restrict candidates to that bit-width.
165	   (`-e signed-integer -b 12` on `wav` is unsupported, so the `-b` is dropped
166	   and the encoding-restricted search runs: with P=24 it yields 24-bit.)
167	3. Among the handler's `write_formats` list, in list order, pick the entry with
168	   the *smallest* precision that is >= P, and when several have equal precision
169	   pick the **last** such entry.  If the input's own encoding appears anywhere in
170	   the list, restrict the search to that encoding first (this is why u-law input
171	   to `wav` gives u-law and not MS-ADPCM, both precision 14).
172	4. If no entry reaches P, pick the entry with the greatest precision, ties going
173	   to the **first** such entry (u-law input, P=14, to `prc` whose candidates are
174	   A-law/8 and IMA-ADPCM/4, both precision 13, gives A-law).
175	
176	## Auto-inserted effects
177	
178	The chain is: `input`, then all user effects in order, then (if needed)
179	`channels`, then `rate`, then `dither`, then `output`.  Verified: the auto
180	`rate`/`channels` always come *after* every user effect, even a user `rate`.
181	
182	`dither` is inserted when the running precision exceeds the output encoding's
183	precision and dithering is not disabled (`-D`).  Running precision is computed
184	by `sox_add_effect` as: unchanged when the handler has `SOX_EFF_MODIFY`
185	(meaning "does not modify samples"), self-computed when it has `SOX_EFF_PREC`,
186	otherwise `SOX_SAMPLE_PRECISION` (32).  Observed consequences:
187	
188	* `st.wav -t s16 -c 4 out` — no dither (channels *up*-mix keeps precision).
189	* `st.wav -t s16 -c 1 out` — dither (down-mix raises precision).
190	* `st.wav -t s16 out reverse` — no dither (`reverse` has SOX_EFF_MODIFY).
191	* `-m` (mix) — dither; `-M` (merge) — no dither.
192	* float output — never dithered.
193	
194	`-G`/`--guard` prepends a `gain` effect (`gain -h`); `--norm` = guard +
195	normalise, which runs the chain into a temporary file and then a second pass.
196	
197	## Miscellaneous
198	
199	* Format options must precede their file name.  Anything after the first
200	  recognised effect name is effect arguments; a stray `-t wav name` there is a
201	  usage error (banner + full usage, exit 1).
202	* An unrecognised word where an effect is expected is treated as a *file name*.
203	* `-n -n` (null input and null output) hangs — never test that.
204	* Default `--buffer` is 8192.
205	* Default output comment is `Processed by SoX`.

#!/bin/sh
# Build ./executable from all sources under src/.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

CC=${CC:-cc}
CFLAGS=${CFLAGS:-"-O2 -std=gnu99 -Wall -Wno-unused-result -Wno-unused-function -Wno-unused-variable -Wno-parentheses -Wno-char-subscripts"}

SRCS=$(find src -name '*.c' | sort)
$CC $CFLAGS -Isrc -o executable $SRCS -lm -lpthread
#!/bin/bash
# compare.sh -- run the reference and our build with identical arguments and
# report any difference in stdout, stderr, exit status or produced files.
#
# Usage: compare.sh [args...]
#   Any argument containing the token @@ is treated as an output file path;
#   @@ is replaced by a per-run scratch directory so the two runs cannot
#   collide, and the resulting files are compared byte-for-byte.
REF=${REF:-/workspace/executable}
OURS=${OURS:-/workspace/executable.new}
[ -x "$OURS" ] || OURS=/workspace/executable.mine

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$TMP/a" "$TMP/b"

argsA=(); argsB=()
for a in "$@"; do
  argsA+=("${a//@@/$TMP/a}")
  argsB+=("${a//@@/$TMP/b}")
done

"$REF"  "${argsA[@]}" >"$TMP/a.out" 2>"$TMP/a.err"; sa=$?
"$OURS" "${argsB[@]}" >"$TMP/b.out" 2>"$TMP/b.err"; sb=$?

# Normalise the program name that appears in diagnostics.
sed -i "s|$REF|SOX|g;s|$TMP/a|DIR|g" "$TMP/a.out" "$TMP/a.err"
sed -i "s|$OURS|SOX|g;s|$TMP/b|DIR|g" "$TMP/b.out" "$TMP/b.err"

rc=0
if [ "$sa" != "$sb" ]; then echo "EXIT: ref=$sa ours=$sb"; rc=1; fi
if ! diff -u "$TMP/a.out" "$TMP/b.out" >"$TMP/d1"; then
  echo "--- stdout differs"; cat "$TMP/d1"; rc=1
fi
if ! diff -u "$TMP/a.err" "$TMP/b.err" >"$TMP/d2"; then
  echo "--- stderr differs"; cat "$TMP/d2"; rc=1
fi
if ! diff -r "$TMP/a" "$TMP/b" >"$TMP/d3" 2>&1; then
  echo "--- output files differ"; cat "$TMP/d3"
  for f in "$TMP"/a/*; do
    b="$TMP/b/$(basename "$f")"
    [ -f "$b" ] || continue
    cmp -l "$f" "$b" | head -20
  done
  rc=1
fi
[ $rc = 0 ] && echo OK
rm -rf "$TMP"
exit $rc

# SoX: Sound eXchange

**The Swiss Army knife of audio manipulation**

## Description

SoX (Sound eXchange) is a command-line audio processing tool that can:
- Read and write audio files in most popular formats
- Apply effects and transformations to audio
- Combine multiple input sources
- Synthesize audio
- Act as a general purpose audio player (when invoked as `play`)
- Act as a multi-track audio recorder (when invoked as `rec`)
- Query audio file metadata (via the `soxi` command)

SoX is particularly suited to making quick, simple edits and batch processing of audio files.

## Usage

### Basic Syntax

```bash
sox [global-options] [format-options] infile1 \
    [[format-options] infile2] ... [format-options] outfile \
    [effect [effect-options]] ...
```

```bash
play [global-options] [format-options] infile1 \
     [[format-options] infile2] ... [format-options] \
     [effect [effect-options]] ...
```

```bash
rec [global-options] [format-options] outfile \
    [effect [effect-options]] ...
```

### Examples

Convert audio format:
```bash
sox recital.au recital.wav
```

Convert with effects (down-mix to mono, resample, fade, normalize):
```bash
sox recital.au -b 16 recital.wav channels 1 rate 16k fade 3 norm
```

Convert raw/headerless audio to WAV:
```bash
sox -r 16k -e signed -b 8 -c 1 voice-memo.raw voice-memo.wav
```

Adjust audio speed:
```bash
sox slow.aiff fixed.aiff speed 1.027
```

Concatenate audio files:
```bash
sox short.wav long.wav longer.wav
```

Mix audio files:
```bash
sox -m music.mp3 voice.wav mixed.flac
```

Play audio with effects:
```bash
play "The Moonbeams/Greatest/*.ogg" bass +3
```

Synthesize audio (A minor seventh chord):
```bash
play -n -c1 synth sin %-12 sin %-9 sin %-5 sin %-2 fade h 0.1 1 0.1
```

Record audio (30 minutes of stereo):
```bash
rec -c 2 radio.aiff trim 0 30:00
```

## SoXI - Query Audio File Information

The `soxi` command displays metadata from audio file headers:

```bash
soxi [options] infile1 ...
```

### Options

- `-t` - Show detected file-type
- `-r` - Show sample-rate
- `-c` - Show number of channels
- `-s` - Show number of samples
- `-d` - Show duration (hours:minutes:seconds)
- `-D` - Show duration in seconds
- `-b` - Show bits per sample
- `-B` - Show bitrate
- `-p` - Show estimated sample precision
- `-e` - Show audio encoding name
- `-a` - Show file comments/annotations

## Supported Audio Formats

SoX supports a wide variety of audio formats including:

- Raw files (various binary and text formats)
- AIFF/AIFC (Apple/SGI)
- AU (SUN, NeXT)
- CDDA (Compact Disc Digital Audio)
- FLAC
- MP2/MP3
- Ogg Vorbis
- Opus
- WAV/RIFX (Microsoft)
- WavPack
- IRCAM SoundFile
- NIST SPHERE
- VOC (SoundBlaster)
- And many more...

## Effects and Processing

SoX includes numerous audio effects:

### Tone/Filter Effects
- Tone generation and synthesis
- Filters (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, etc.)
- Equalizer effects

### Volume/Dynamics
- Volume adjustment
- Normalization
- Companding/compression
- Gain control
- Fade in/out

### Temporal Effects
- Delay and echo
- Reverb
- Chorus and flanger
- Phaser
- Tremolo

### Editing
- Trim
- Pad
- Silence detection/removal
- Splice
- Reverse

### Analysis
- Statistics
- Spectrograms
- Voice activity detection

### Other
- Rate conversion/resampling
- Channel mixing and remixing
- Dithering
- Format conversion

## Documentation

For complete details on usage, effects, and supported formats, consult the manual pages:
- `man sox` - Main command documentation
- `man soxi` - File information tool documentation
- `man soxformat` - Supported formats and devices
- `man libsox` - Library API documentation

## License

SoX is licensed under the GNU GPL and GNU LGPL.

The `sox` and `soxi` programs are distributed under the GPL, while the library `libsox` 
(in which most of SoX's functionality resides) is dual-licensed. Some optional components 
of libsox are GPL only.

See the LICENSE files for details.

## Project Information

- Website: http://sox.sourceforge.net
- Mailing list: sox-users@lists.sourceforge.net
- Bug reports: sox-devel@lists.sourceforge.net
